newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbek foreign trade bank boosts capital to $470 mln.
newsitem.headline: Uzbek foreign trade bank boosts capital to $470 mln.

text.p: TASHKENT, Jan 29 (Reuetr) - Uzbekistan's National Bank for Foreign Economic Activity has boosted its charter capital to $470 million from $200 million, a bank press release said.
"This brings the bank into the group of the world's 500 best capitalised banks," the statement said.

"The increase in charter capital will not only enable the bank to fulfil its role in structural reforms that take place in main sectors of the economy, such as mining, textile, agriculture and energy but will also improve conditions for foreign and domestic investors," the statement said.
The bank, set up in September 1991 to serve Uzbekistan's foreign trade, also said its unaudited operational profits rose 30 percent last year to $102 million from $79 million in 1995.
The total balance sheet rose to $3.4 billion, from $1.8 billion in 1995.

"The increase in the results of the bank reflects the growth of the Uzbek economy in 1996 and even better results may be expected in 1997 since the industrial base of Uzbekistan will continue to expand, mainly through the processing of mineral and agricultural raw materials," the press release said.
